text:
maria-r: Heads up — quick canary smoke for the new int8 variant on raven-lite. Seeing ~0.8% of toolcall responses fail JSON schema (mostly truncated arrays / trailing commas) when streaming + kv-cache enabled. Sampled 10k requests.
alex_w: ow. is that concentrated on long contexts or short ones?
maria-r: mostly mid-length (1k-3k tokens). Noticing failures right at stream chunk boundaries in the logs. Example payloads attached below.
sam: can you paste a raw example? even a minimal truncated output helps.
maria-r: ```\n{"action": "search", "args": ["openai models"],\n{"action": "rank", "args": ["doc1", "doc2"]}\n```\n(so you see an accidental splice where an object starts after a newline and we end up with malformed JSON sequence)
jen: interesting. could be a tokenizer/stream framing mismatch after quantized kernels change chunk sizes. any difference vs fp16 canary?
maria-r: fp16 baseline had ~0.02% parse failures. int8 jump to ~0.8%. same prompt set and batching settings.
alex_w: do we have streaming boundary offsets telemetry? i.e., token offsets per chunk and where we flush the buffer
jen: yes, we have a proto metric: `stream_chunk_end_token` and `kv_cache_prefix_len` per request. i can slice by those.
sam: theory: quantization changed subtoken alignment -> stream flush lands in middle of multibyte token -> decoder emits weird bytes that our serializer escapes badly -> JSON broken. but also could be batch reordering.
maria-r: repro plan: 1) replay failing requests with deterministic seeding (no burst batching), 2) run with streaming disabled to check if only streaming related, 3) run with kv-cache disabled. anyone available to pair on 1?
alex_w: I can take replay 1 today. where's the failing request dump?
maria-r: uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-canaries/int8-json-smoke/1725000000/failures.tar.gz
infra-bot: Deploy bot: Canary job `int8-canary-v3` started on pool-7c. Job id: #3412. Logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/canaries/3412
jen: quick ask: add a sampling flag to also save the raw token stream (not just reconstructed text) for a subset of runs — that'll help see framing.
sam: +1. also add a side-by-side run with `--quant-kernel=legacy` when replaying.
alex_w: grabbing the tar now. will run isolated replay with streaming off and post results in ~30m.
maria-r: thanks. if replay reproduces, we should consider an immediate heuristics patch: on parse errors, try simple NDJSON recovery (wrap lines and attempt per-line parse) and an exponential retry backoff that increases non-streaming fallback probability.
jen: note we must track unit-economic impact of falling back to non-streaming (latency token cost). add a metric for fallback_rate and median_p50_latency_post_fallback.
sam: also add a canary that runs QA evals (toolcall acceptance) on a 2k prompt sample before enabling int8 to prod.
alex_w: update: isolated replay with streaming disabled -> parse failures drop to 0.01% (close to fp16). streaming enabled repros ~0.74%. posting logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/canary/3412/replay
maria-r: good repro. next step: collect token-stream diffs for 500 random repros and run tokenizer alignment check.
jen: will schedule telemetry slice for that. tagging infra to increase retention for those runs.
sam: if alignment check shows multibyte split, we can try adjusting stream flush to ensure UTF-8 safe boundaries (simple heuristic: back up until valid UTF-8 sequence). might fix quickly.
maria-r: ok let's reconvene after alex posts diffs. thanks all :thumbsup:
